Second, "enkodieren/Enkodierung" (lines 34, 36, 40, 380, 828) alternates with plain "kodieren/kodiert" (lines 34, 822) — "enkodieren" is an unnecessary anglicism a German technical writer would render "kodieren/codieren". Third, one grammar slip in a counterfactual: line 405 "wenn wir … ausführen würden, optimieren wir ihn wie zuvor" uses the indicative apodosis where "würden wir ihn … optimieren" is required. None of these mislead; the concept stays identifiable in each case.

examples.source: Now that we have a kernel matrix and a similarly formatted test_matrix from quantum kernel methods…
examples.translation: Nachdem wir nun eine Kernel-Matrix und eine ähnlich formatierte test_matrix aus den Quanten-Kernel-Methoden haben…
examples.suggested: Nachdem wir nun eine Kernmatrix und eine ähnlich formatierte test_matrix aus den Quantenkernel-Methoden haben…
examples.why: The file establishes "Kernmatrix" (~30 occurrences) and "Quantenkernel-Methode" (title, sidebar_label, intro); lines 311/482/492 switch to "Kernel-Matrix" and "Quanten-Kernel-Methoden", so the same object carries two names within one lesson.

examples.source: …attempts to use a quantum circuit that has very high two-qubit depth…
examples.translation: …versucht, eine Quantenschaltung mit sehr hoher Zwei-Qubit-Tiefe zu verwenden…
examples.suggested: …versucht, einen Quantenschaltkreis mit sehr hoher Zwei-Qubit-Tiefe zu verwenden…
examples.why: "Schaltkreis" is the convention everywhere else in the file (Quantenschaltkreis, Schaltkreistiefe, Overlap-Schaltkreis); "Quantenschaltung"/"dieser Schaltung" appears only in this one exercise paragraph.

examples.source: You can construct your own circuit to encode your data…
examples.translation: Du kannst deinen eigenen Schaltkreis zum Enkodieren deiner Daten bauen…
examples.suggested: Du kannst deinen eigenen Schaltkreis zum Kodieren deiner Daten bauen…
examples.why: "enkodieren/Enkodierung" is a calque on "encode"; the same file already writes "die Daten in einen Quantenschaltkreis zu kodieren" (line 34) and "auf N Bits kodiert" (line 822), so the natural German term is present but not used consistently.

examples.source: We will construct an overlap circuit, and if we were running on a real quantum computer in this example, we would optimize it for execution as before.
examples.translation: Wir erstellen einen Overlap-Schaltkreis, und wenn wir in diesem Beispiel auf einem realen Quantencomputer ausführen würden, optimieren wir ihn wie zuvor für die Ausführung.
examples.suggested: …würden wir ihn wie zuvor für die Ausführung optimieren.
examples.why: The English is counterfactual (they are NOT running on hardware here); the German main clause slips into the indicative, which reads as if the optimization does happen. The following sentences ("In diesem Fall beabsichtigen wir jedoch…") still make the setup clear, so this is stiffness/grammar rather than misleading content.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no semantic drift, no hallucinated claim, and every load-bearing passage survives intact (the "erkennt jedoch weder direkt vertikale Linien noch vollständig horizontale Linien, da die untere Zeile ignoriert wird" reasoning, the barren-plateau caveat "nicht die einzige Überlegung", the 60%/100% accuracy narrative, the "ca. 60 % niedriger" loss claim, and the closing "72 freie Parameter … um mindestens einen Faktor 2–3 reduziert"). Register is consistently informal du (zero Sie/Ihnen forms). What a native editor would change is terminology consistency: "variational" is rendered three ways — "variativ" (line 19, twice), "variationell" (lines 147, 155, 177, 243) and "Quantenvariations-" (title) — and "circuit" splits down the middle of the document, "Quantenschaltkreis/Schaltkreis" in the first half versus English "Circuit / Quantum Circuit / Variational Circuit" from "Das Modell verbessern" (line 645) onward, plus one stray "Schaltung" (line 395) and one "Gattern" (line 871) against "Gates" everywhere else; "Optimierer" (4×) alternates with "Optimizer" (2×), and "Quantenklassifizierer" (19) with "Quantenklassifikator" (147). Smaller: the "### Data" heading (line 869) was left untranslated while every other heading was translated, "vernünftig voneinander getrennt" (264) is a calque of "reasonably well separated", "die Optimierungsschritte zu verlängern" (619) misreads the idiom "extending the optimization steps", and "CNOT Gates" appears unhyphenated 3× (651) against "CNOT-Gates" 5×.

examples.source: variational quantum circuits … variational quantum classifiers (VQCs) … This variational circuit is sometimes called the "ansatz".
examples.translation: variative Quantenschaltkreise … variative Quantenklassifizierer (VQCs) [19] … ## Variationeller Quantenklassifikator [147] … Dieser variationelle Schaltkreis [155] … # Quantenvariationsschaltkreise [17]
examples.suggested: Settle on one convention throughout, e.g. "variationelle Quantenschaltkreise" / "variationeller Quantenklassifikator", and use it in the title too.
examples.why: "variativ" is not the established German rendering for "variational" in the QC literature, and the file mixes it with the correct "variationell" plus a compound "Quantenvariations-" in the H1. The concept stays identifiable, so this is MINOR, but it is the most visible slip in the file.

examples.source: circuit depth … our previous variational circuit … non-Clifford gates
examples.translation: "Hier optimieren wir die Schaltung …" [395]; "ist die Circuit-Tiefe ein wesentlicher Aspekt" [600]; "beim ersten Variational Circuit" [645]; "Unser vorheriger Variational Circuit" [651]; "Nicht-Clifford-Gattern" [871]
examples.suggested: Keep "Quantenschaltkreis"/"Schaltkreis" (used consistently up to line 437) throughout, or commit to the English "Circuit" everywhere; likewise "Gates" rather than a one-off "Gattern".
examples.why: The document switches convention roughly halfway through: the first half translates circuit, the second half keeps the English word, with a single "Schaltung" in between. A German technical editor would unify this; it does not mislead.

examples.source: The eigenvalues of Z (±1) are reasonably well separated, and result in an estimator outcome in interval [-1, +1]
examples.translation: Die Eigenwerte von $Z$ ($\pm 1$) sind vernünftig voneinander getrennt und führen zu einem Estimator-Ergebnis im Intervall [-1, +1]
examples.suggested: Die Eigenwerte von $Z$ ($\pm 1$) liegen hinreichend weit auseinander und führen zu einem Estimator-Ergebnis im Intervall [-1, +1]
examples.why: "vernünftig getrennt" is a word-for-word calque of "reasonably separated"; in German "vernünftig" means "sensible/rational", not "sufficiently". Meaning still comes across, but no native technical writer would phrase it this way.

examples.source: We might try extending the optimization steps to make sure the optimizer didn't just get stuck in a local minimum
examples.translation: Wir könnten versuchen, die Optimierungsschritte zu verlängern, um sicherzustellen, dass der Optimizer nicht in einem lokalen Minimum des Parameterraums steckengeblieben ist.
examples.suggested: Wir könnten versuchen, die Zahl der Optimierungsschritte zu erhöhen, um sicherzustellen, dass der Optimierer nicht bloß in einem lokalen Minimum des Parameterraums hängengeblieben ist.
examples.why: "Schritte verlängern" reads as making each step longer rather than running more of them; the English means more iterations. Also "Optimizer" here vs "Optimierer" at lines 332 and 362.

examples.source: ### Data
examples.translation: ### Data {#data}
examples.suggested: ### Daten {#data}
examples.why: Every other heading in the file is translated ("### Verlustfunktion", "### Testen und Genauigkeit", "### Abschluss"); this one was left in English, so the section list reads inconsistently to a German reader.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked every claim-bearing sentence (superposition "bedeutet nicht, dass du beide Ergebnisse in einer einzigen Messung siehst", the 50/50 |00⟩/|11⟩ answer, "mehr Shots bedeuten ein höheres Signal-Rausch-Verhältnis", the simulator section's "ohne Vorkommnisse von $01$ oder $10$", and the Ψ⁻ closing hint) and found no inverted condition, swapped quantity or dropped caveat; core terminology is correct and consistent (Verschränkung, Superpositionszustand, Bell-Zustand, Shots, Counts, Kontroll-/Ziel-Qubit, Transpilieren, Sampler-Primitive). What a native technical editor would still change is fluency and typography: line 30 "Um auf einem echten IBM Quantencomputer auszuführen" is a bare calque of "To run on…" and is missing its object ("Um es … auszuführen"); the compounds "Messung-Histogramm" (l. 122) and "Qubit-Messung-Histogramm" (l. 266) are non-German formations where "Messhistogramm" / "Messhistogramm der Qubits" is the normal term; "die Rauschen aufnehmen können" (l. 177) literalizes "pick up noise" instead of "die Rauschen ausgesetzt sind"; and "oder es lokal betreiben" (l. 24) uses the wrong verb for a notebook. Separately, the German opening quote „ is closed with an ASCII straight " in five places (l. 89, 91, 104, 118, 215) while l. 246 gets „perfekt“ right — inconsistent typography, not a meaning defect. Register is correct informal du throughout with no Sie slips.

examples.source: To run on a real IBM quantum computer, you'll also need a (free) IBM Quantum® Platform account.
examples.translation: Um auf einem echten IBM Quantencomputer auszuführen, benötigst du außerdem ein (kostenloses) IBM Quantum® Platform-Konto.
examples.suggested: Um es auf einem echten IBM Quantencomputer auszuführen, benötigst du außerdem ein (kostenloses) IBM Quantum® Platform-Konto.
examples.why: Direct calque of English intransitive 'to run on'; German 'ausführen' requires an object, so the clause reads as raw MT and is grammatically incomplete.

examples.source: the measurement histogram of your Hello World circuit / a correlation in the qubit measurement histogram
examples.translation: das Messung-Histogramm deines Hello World Circuits / die Verschränkung als Korrelation im Qubit-Messung-Histogramm
examples.suggested: das Messhistogramm deines Hello-World-Circuits / die Verschränkung als Korrelation im Messhistogramm der Qubits
examples.why: 'Messung-Histogramm' and 'Qubit-Messung-Histogramm' are non-native compounds built word-for-word from English; German forms the compound with the stem ('Messhistogramm').

examples.source: IBM QPUs are physical systems that can pick up noise, so gates are slightly imperfect…
examples.translation: IBM QPUs sind physikalische Systeme, die Rauschen aufnehmen können, sodass Gates leicht unvollkommen sind…
examples.suggested: IBM QPUs sind physikalische Systeme, die Rauschen ausgesetzt sind, sodass Gates leicht unvollkommen sind…
examples.why: 'Rauschen aufnehmen' literalizes 'pick up noise' and suggests recording noise rather than being subject to it; meaning is still recoverable from context, so minor.

examples.source: You can run this notebook from top to bottom in a fresh Google Colab runtime, or run locally.
examples.translation: Du kannst dieses Notebook von oben nach unten in einer neuen Google Colab-Laufzeitumgebung ausführen oder es lokal betreiben.
examples.suggested: … ausführen oder es lokal laufen lassen.
examples.why: 'betreiben' is used for operating a system or service, not for running a notebook; a German technical writer would not switch verbs mid-sentence here.

examples.source: the "Hello World" circuit / the red box labeled "H" / a "perfect world" version
examples.translation: des „Hello World"-Circuits / mit der Bezeichnung „H" / eine „perfekte Welt"-Version
examples.suggested: des „Hello World“-Circuits / mit der Bezeichnung „H“ / eine „perfekte Welt“-Version
examples.why: German opening quote „ is closed with an ASCII straight quote in five places, while line 246 correctly writes „perfekt“ — inconsistent quotation typography within the same file.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the load-bearing physics survives intact: the CNOT condition ("kippt Qubit 1 … nur, wenn Qubit 0 … sich im Zustand |1⟩ befindet"), the normalization/probability chain, the "deterministisch und reversibel" vs. "von Natur aus zufällig und irreversibel" contrast, the superposition caveat ("eine philosophische Interpretation, die nicht getestet werden kann"), and the glued-coins entanglement analogy are all correct, and the last 40% (Pauli/Observable, Bell-circuit walkthrough, Fazit) shows no drift or hallucination. What a native technical editor would change is surface: "das rechteste Qubit" / "das linkeste Qubit" are not German superlatives (native: "das am weitesten rechts/links stehende Qubit"); "flip" is rendered inconsistently — "kippt Qubit 1" for CNOT but "**Pauli-Y** vertauscht das Qubit", where "vertauschen" with a single object is wrong (should be "kippt"/"invertiert"); "in jede Richtung im dreidimensionalen Raum zeigt" reads as "in every direction" where EN means "in eine beliebige Richtung"; and two calques ("Lass uns diesen Bell-Zustand-Circuit zurückbringen", plus a missing reflexive in "die Quantencomputer anders als klassische Computer verhalten lassen"). Register is informal "du" as required, though it drifts to impersonal "man" in the measurement-basis sections.

examples.source: This means that the rightmost qubit is considered the first (or least significant) qubit, and the leftmost qubit is the most significant qubit.
examples.translation: Das bedeutet, dass das rechteste Qubit als das erste (oder am wenigsten signifikante) Qubit betrachtet wird und das linkeste Qubit das signifikanteste Qubit ist.
examples.suggested: Das bedeutet, dass das am weitesten rechts stehende Qubit als das erste (oder niederwertigste) Qubit gilt und das am weitesten links stehende Qubit das höchstwertige ist.
examples.why: "rechteste"/"linkeste" are not valid German superlatives of rechts/links; a native technical writer uses "am weitesten rechts/links stehend" (and "nieder-/höchstwertig" for least/most significant). Repeats in the following two bullets ("das rechteste Bit", "das linkeste Bit"). Meaning is still recoverable, so MINOR.

examples.source: **Pauli-Y** flips the qubit and introduces a phase.
examples.translation: **Pauli-Y** vertauscht das Qubit und führt eine Phase ein.
examples.suggested: **Pauli-Y** kippt das Qubit und führt eine Phase ein.
examples.why: "vertauschen" needs two objects (it works in the Pauli-X bullet, which swaps |0⟩ and |1⟩), but with a single qubit it is wrong — the operation flips it. The same verb "flip" is rendered "kippt" in the CNOT paragraph ("Das CNOT-Gate kippt Qubit 1"), so the file is internally inconsistent.

examples.source: A superposition of |0⟩ and |1⟩ will result in a state vector that points in any direction in three-dimensional space
examples.translation: Eine Superposition von $\vert 0\rangle$ und $\vert 1\rangle$ führt zu einem Zustandsvektor, der in jede Richtung im dreidimensionalen Raum zeigt
examples.suggested: … führt zu einem Zustandsvektor, der in eine beliebige Richtung im dreidimensionalen Raum zeigen kann
examples.why: English "any direction" is "eine beliebige Richtung"; "in jede Richtung … zeigt" reads as the vector pointing in every direction at once. The following clause ("die genaue Richtung hängt von den relativen Amplituden und Phasen ab") lets the learner recover the intended sense, so MINOR rather than misleading.

examples.source: Many of the quantum phenomena that make quantum computers behave differently from classical computers are already present in the deceptively simple Bell state we produced in the previous lesson. Let's bring back that Bell state circuit:
examples.translation: Viele der Quantenphänomene, die Quantencomputer anders als klassische Computer verhalten lassen, sind bereits im täuschend einfachen Bell-Zustand vorhanden … Lass uns diesen Bell-Zustand-Circuit zurückbringen:
examples.suggested: Viele der Quantenphänomene, die dafür sorgen, dass sich Quantencomputer anders verhalten als klassische Computer, … Rufen wir uns diesen Bell-Zustands-Circuit noch einmal in Erinnerung:
examples.why: Two calques in one paragraph: "verhalten lassen" is missing the reflexive "sich" (sich verhalten) and reads as raw English syntax, and "zurückbringen" literalizes "bring back" — German would say "noch einmal ansehen" / "in Erinnerung rufen".

examples.source: By default, when you measure a qubit in a quantum circuit … So how, in practice, do you measure in the X or Y basis?
examples.translation: Standardmäßig misst man beim Messen eines Qubits in einem Quantum-Circuit … Wie misst man also in der Praxis in der X- oder Y-Basis? … Daher musst du die Basis wechseln
examples.suggested: Standardmäßig misst du beim Messen eines Qubits … Wie misst du also in der Praxis in der X- oder Y-Basis?
examples.why: The file's convention is informal "du" (used in the intro, the exercises and the Fazit), but the two measurement-basis sections switch to impersonal "man" and then back to "du" within the same paragraph. No Sie-forms appear, so this is a consistency slip, not a register failure.

editor_note: One inverted instruction makes this FAIL: the English "you can uncomment and run this cell instead" becomes "kannst du stattdessen diese Zelle auskommentieren und ausführen" — in German "auskommentieren" means to COMMENT OUT, the exact opposite; a learner told to comment out an already fully commented simulator cell and run it gets nothing and cannot follow the alternative simulator path (correct: "die Auskommentierung dieser Zelle aufheben"). The rest of the file is otherwise faithful and readable, with correct, consistent domain terms (Superposition, Verschränkung, Observablen, Grundzustand, Transpiler, transversales Feld, Hamiltonian kept in English form throughout) and a consistent informal "du". Remaining defects are minor: the malformed comparative "herausforderndererem", the misspelling "Fehlerminimirungs- und -unterdrückungstechniken" (vs. correct "Fehlerminimierung" a paragraph later), "niedrigst möglichen" for "niedrigstmöglichen", the dropped modality in "bevorzugen sie es" for "they might prefer to align", and "variationaler Methoden" against "Variationsmethoden"/"Variationsalgorithmen" elsewhere in the same file.

examples.source: Or, if you're using a simulator, you can uncomment and run this cell instead:
examples.translation: Oder, wenn du einen Simulator verwendest, kannst du stattdessen diese Zelle auskommentieren und ausführen:
examples.suggested: Oder, wenn du einen Simulator verwendest, kannst du bei dieser Zelle stattdessen die Auskommentierung aufheben und sie ausführen:
examples.why: Inverted instruction: 'auskommentieren' = comment out, the opposite of 'uncomment'. The cell in question is entirely commented-out code; following the German literally leaves the simulator path dead and teaches the wrong action.

examples.source: Optionally implement error mitigation and suppression techniques to reduce the effects of noise.
examples.translation: Implementieren wir optional Fehlerminimirungs- und -unterdrückungstechniken, um die Auswirkungen von Rauschen zu reduzieren.
examples.suggested: Implementieren wir optional Techniken zur Fehlerminimierung und Fehlerunterdrückung, um die Auswirkungen von Rauschen zu reduzieren.
examples.why: 'Fehlerminimirungs-' is misspelled (missing 'e'), and the same concept is spelled correctly as 'Fehlerminimierung' one paragraph later — an inconsistency inside the same section.

examples.source: We'll focus on the latter case because it often leads to more interesting — and more challenging — behavior.
examples.translation: Wir konzentrieren uns auf den letzteren Fall, weil er oft zu interessanterem — und herausforderndererem — Verhalten führt.
examples.suggested: … weil er oft zu interessanterem – und anspruchsvollerem – Verhalten führt.
examples.why: 'herausforderndererem' is a malformed double comparative that does not exist in German; no native technical writer would produce it.

examples.source: Depending on the sign of their interaction, they might prefer to align and point in the same direction, or anti-align …
examples.translation: Abhängig vom Vorzeichen ihrer Wechselwirkung bevorzugen sie es, sich auszurichten und in dieselbe Richtung zu zeigen, oder sich anti-auszurichten …
examples.suggested: … kann es sein, dass sie sich ausrichten und in dieselbe Richtung zeigen, oder sich anti-ausrichten …
examples.why: The hedge 'might' is dropped, turning a conditional possibility into a flat assertion; minor strengthening of the claim.

examples.source: This approach is the essence of variational methods … go beyond variational techniques.
examples.translation: Dieser Ansatz ist das Wesen variationaler Methoden … die über Variationsmethoden hinausgehen.
examples.suggested: Use 'Variationsmethoden' (or 'variationelle Methoden') consistently.
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency: 'variationaler Methoden' (nonstandard form) two sentences before 'Variationsmethoden', with 'Variationsalgorithmen' used earlier in the lesson.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no semantic drift, no inverted condition, no swapped quantity and no hallucinated sentence; the load-bearing passages (CNOT "kippt das Zielqubit nur dann, wenn das Steuerqubit $|1\rangle$ ist", the 75%-Chance example, the Little-Endian note, the depth-4/depth-5 explanations, the closing paragraph on Qubit-Konnektivität) all match the English exactly, and the "du"-register holds without a single Sie-slip. What a native technical editor would still change: (1) "single-qubit" is rendered two ways in the same file — the compound "Einzelqubit-Gates / Einzelqubit-Schaltkreis / Einzelqubit-Fall" (lines 130, 344, 427, 693) versus the calqued adjective form "Einzelne Qubit-Gates" (l. 31), "Einzelnes Qubit-Gate" (heading 3, l. 47), "Einzelner Qubit-Quantenzustand" (heading 3.2, l. 330, and l. 98), where the German literally reads "one gate on a qubit" rather than "single-qubit gate"; (2) "inner product space" is rendered "Innenproduktraum" (l. 82), a calque — the conventional German is "Skalarproduktraum" (or "innerer Produktraum"/"Prähilbertraum"); (3) "das rechteste Bit" / "das linkeste Bit" (l. 666) and "einige Literatur im Quantencomputing verwendet" are English-shaped constructions no German technical writer would use; (4) "die obige Superposition mit gleicher Wahrscheinlichkeit vorbereitet" (l. 585) is momentarily ambiguous (reads as "prepares with equal probability" rather than "the equal-probability superposition"); (5) minor stiffness: "auf den $|0\rangle$" (l. 265), "dessen Aktion zwei Qubits gleichzeitig einbezieht" (l. 758, Aktion→Wirkung), doubled "Obwohl … Obwohl" (l. 629). None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: Single-qubit quantum gate / Single-qubit quantum state / Single-qubit gates
examples.translation: Einzelnes Qubit-Gate / Einzelner Qubit-Quantenzustand / Einzelne Qubit-Gates
examples.suggested: Einzelqubit-Gate / Einzelqubit-Quantenzustand / Einzelqubit-Gates
examples.why: The file already uses the correct compound elsewhere ("Einzelqubit-Gates" l. 344/427, "Einzelqubit-Schaltkreis" l. 130, "Einzelqubit-Fall" l. 693). The adjective form in the headings parses as "a single gate" / "a single quantum state" instead of "single-qubit", so the same concept is split two ways within one file.

examples.source: a unit vector in a two-dimensional complex inner product space with an orthonormal basis of |0> and |1>
examples.translation: ein Einheitsvektor in einem zweidimensionalen komplexen Innenproduktraum mit einer orthonormalen Basis aus |0> und |1>
examples.suggested: … in einem zweidimensionalen komplexen Skalarproduktraum (bzw. innerem Produktraum) …
examples.why: "Innenproduktraum" is a literal calque; German mathematics and quantum-information texts say "Skalarproduktraum", "innerer Produktraum" or "Prähilbertraum". Recognizable, so MINOR, but not the conventional term.

examples.source: qubit 0 is the rightmost bit … some literature in quantum computing use the Big Endian notation (qubit 0 is the leftmost bit)
examples.translation: Qubit 0 das rechteste Bit … einige Literatur im Quantencomputing verwendet die Big-Endian-Notation (Qubit 0 ist das linkeste Bit)
examples.suggested: Qubit 0 das am weitesten rechts stehende Bit … ein Teil der Literatur zum Quantencomputing verwendet die Big-Endian-Notation (Qubit 0 ist das am weitesten links stehende Bit)
examples.why: "rechteste"/"linkeste" are non-idiomatic superlatives and "einige Literatur" is a direct calque of "some literature" (German uses "ein Teil der Literatur" / "manche Quellen"). Meaning survives; the sentence reads as machine output.

examples.source: Next, let's measure a circuit that prepares the equal probability superposition above.
examples.translation: Als Nächstes messen wir einen Schaltkreis, der die obige Superposition mit gleicher Wahrscheinlichkeit vorbereitet.
examples.suggested: Als Nächstes messen wir einen Schaltkreis, der die oben gezeigte gleichwahrscheinliche Superposition präpariert.
examples.why: As written, "mit gleicher Wahrscheinlichkeit" attaches to "vorbereitet" and momentarily reads as "prepares with equal probability" rather than qualifying the superposition. Also "präparieren" is the standard verb for state preparation in German quantum texts.

examples.source: applying a quantum gate to the qubit evolves the quantum state / its action involves two qubits at once / So while we expect roughly a 50-50 distribution
examples.translation: dass die Anwendung eines Quanten-Gates auf das Qubit den Quantenzustand entwickelt / dessen Aktion zwei Qubits gleichzeitig einbezieht / Obwohl wir ungefähr eine 50-50-Verteilung erwarten (directly after "Obwohl hier kein Rauschen simuliert wurde")
examples.suggested: … den Quantenzustand zeitlich weiterentwickelt / dessen Wirkung zwei Qubits gleichzeitig betrifft / Wir erwarten zwar ungefähr eine 50-50-Verteilung, werden sie aber selten genau antreffen
examples.why: Three small stiffness/calque points: bare "entwickelt" for "evolves" is unclear without "zeitlich", "Aktion" is an anglicism where German uses "Wirkung", and two consecutive sentences opening with "Obwohl" reads mechanically. Nothing here changes the meaning.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination: the compute-uncompute explanation ("in der er umgekehrt wird $U^\dagger$", ideal outcome $|000000\rangle$), the "$4k$ Zwei-Qubit-Gate-Schichten" note, the resilience-level labels and the "Stand 28.06.2024" caveat all match the English exactly, and the informal "du" register holds consistently (Beachte, Passe, Probiere, findest du). What a native technical editor would still change is surface German: in the Admonition the separable verb is stranded — "[Lade das PDF herunter](…) der ursprünglichen Vorlesung" leaves the genitive attribute dangling after "herunter" and is ungrammatical; correct is "[Lade das PDF](…) der ursprünglichen Vorlesung herunter." In §2.2 "Zunächst müssen wir Quanten- (oder Auslesefehler) definieren" mis-sets the parenthesis so the suspended hyphen has nothing to attach to — it should be "Quanten- (oder Auslese-)Fehler". Two smaller slips: "6-Qubit-Trotterisierte Circuits" (§3) is a calqued English compound where German wants "trotterisierte 6-Qubit-Circuits", and "X-Gates `d` mal wiederholen" (§2.1) should be "`d`-mal". None of these mislead a learner; terminology (Fehlerminderung, Rauschmodell, Erwartungswerte, Observable, transpilieren, Shots, Estimator/Sampler) is correct and consistent.

examples.source: [Download the pdf](…) of the original lecture.
examples.translation: [Lade das PDF herunter](…) der ursprünglichen Vorlesung.
examples.suggested: [Lade das PDF](…) der ursprünglichen Vorlesung herunter.
examples.why: The separable prefix "herunter" was pulled into the link text, stranding the genitive attribute after it. The result is not grammatical German word order; a native writer would place "herunter" at the end of the clause.

examples.source: We first need to define quantum (or readout) errors to add to a noise model.
examples.translation: Zunächst müssen wir Quanten- (oder Auslesefehler) definieren, die dem Rauschmodell hinzugefügt werden sollen.
examples.suggested: Zunächst müssen wir Quanten- (oder Auslese-)Fehler definieren, die dem Rauschmodell hinzugefügt werden sollen.
examples.why: The parenthesis was placed around the whole word, so the suspended hyphen in "Quanten-" has no head noun to bind to. German requires "Quanten- (oder Auslese-)Fehler".

examples.source: We consider 6-qubit Trotterized circuits for simulating the time evolution of one dimensional Ising model
examples.translation: Wir betrachten 6-Qubit-Trotterisierte Circuits zur Simulation der Zeitentwicklung des eindimensionalen Ising-Modells
examples.suggested: Wir betrachten trotterisierte 6-Qubit-Circuits zur Simulation der Zeitentwicklung des eindimensionalen Ising-Modells
examples.why: English adjective stacking calqued into a German compound: a capitalized participle glued into the middle of a hyphenated noun chain. German puts the participial adjective in front of the compound.

examples.source: toy 1-qubit circuits which just repeat X gates `d` times
examples.translation: einfache 1-Qubit-Circuits, die X-Gates `d` mal wiederholen
examples.suggested: einfache 1-Qubit-Circuits, die X-Gates `d`-mal wiederholen
examples.why: Multiplicative "-mal" attaches with a hyphen to a symbol/variable in German orthography ("`d`-mal", like "25-fache" used correctly later in §2.7); the free-standing "`d` mal" is an English spacing calque.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: the O(N)/O(√N) claim, "vier Hauptkomponenten", the ≈√N repetitions of Orakel+Diffusionsoperator, "zwei Iterationen sind optimal … nicht 100 %", and the closing three-observation arc (höchste → leicht abgenommen → niedrigste Wahrscheinlichkeit) all match the English exactly, and the informal "du" register (Beachte, Betrachte, Importiere, Lass uns) holds without a single Sie-slip. Three things a native technical editor would still fix: (1) "Diese Phaseinvertierung" is a malformed compound — German requires the linking -n-, i.e. "Phaseninvertierung" (or better "Dieser Phasenflip"); (2) the PDF link sentence "[Das PDF herunterladen] der ursprünglichen Vorlesung" is ungrammatical word order once the link text is inlined — the genitive dangles after the separable verb; (3) in the 4-element example the relative pronoun "der" in "den Index des Elements dar, der diese Bedingung erfüllt" attaches to *Index* rather than to *Element* (which would need "das"), so it reads as if the index, not the element, satisfies the condition. Terminology is otherwise correct and consistent (Orakel, Diffusionsoperator, Amplitudenverstärkung, Überlagerung, Phasen-Kickback, Hilfs-Qubit, transpilieren).

examples.source: This phase flip is achieved by applying a negative sign to the amplitude of the target state via phase kickback.
examples.translation: Diese Phaseinvertierung wird durch das Anwenden eines negativen Vorzeichens auf die Amplitude des Zielzustands über Phasen-Kickback erreicht.
examples.suggested: Diese Phaseninvertierung wird erreicht, indem der Amplitude des Zielzustands über Phasen-Kickback ein negatives Vorzeichen gegeben wird.
examples.why: "Phaseinvertierung" is not a well-formed German compound — the Fugen-n is obligatory ("Phasen-"), as the file itself uses correctly two lines earlier in "Phasen-Kickback" and in "Phasenverschiebung". The nominalised "durch das Anwenden" is also stiff next to a verbal clause.

examples.source: [Download the pdf](…) of the original lecture.
examples.translation: [Das PDF herunterladen](…) der ursprünglichen Vorlesung.
examples.suggested: [Das PDF der ursprünglichen Vorlesung herunterladen](…).
examples.why: With the link text inlined the sentence reads "Das PDF herunterladen der ursprünglichen Vorlesung" — a separable-verb infinitive followed by a dangling genitive, which is ungrammatical in German. Pulling the genitive inside the link text (or restructuring to "Hier kannst du das PDF … herunterladen") fixes it.

examples.source: the quantum state |01⟩ represents the index of the element that satisfies this condition
examples.translation: stellt der Quantenzustand $|01\rangle$ den Index des Elements dar, der diese Bedingung erfüllt
examples.suggested: stellt der Quantenzustand $|01\rangle$ den Index desjenigen Elements dar, das diese Bedingung erfüllt
examples.why: "der" is masculine and therefore binds to "Index", not to the neuter "Elements" — so the German literally says the *index* satisfies the condition. "das" (plus "desjenigen") restores the English attachment. Does not mislead badly (the surrounding sentence disambiguates), but a native editor would correct it.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and the "du"-register holds consistently (Beachte, passe den Backend-Namen an, Vergleiche das Ergebnis); core terms (Qubit, Gate, Backend/Target, Coupling Map, Verschränkungs-Gate, Auslesefehler) are correct and stable. Four editorial slips: (1) the coupling-map sentence says edges show which pairs "mit dem 2-Qubit-Verschränkungs-Gate verbunden werden können" — the English says the gate can be *applied to* those pairs, not that the pairs are connected *by* it, so the mental picture is slightly off; (2) "median errors" is rendered "die mittleren Fehler" in §3.2 while the same concept is correctly "Median der T1-Zeiten"/"Median der T2-Zeiten" earlier — "mittlere" reads as arithmetic mean and clashes with the adjacent statistics.median code; (3) the second "tend to" hedge is dropped ("die wiederum größer sind" instead of "in der Regel größer"); (4) "A popular feature" is strengthened to "Ein besonders beliebtes Feature". None of these teaches a false concept, so this stays MINOR.

examples.source: Edges indicate pairs to which you can directly apply the 2-qubit entangling gate.
examples.translation: Kanten zeigen an, welche Paare direkt mit dem 2-Qubit-Verschränkungs-Gate verbunden werden können.
examples.suggested: Kanten zeigen die Paare an, auf die du das 2-Qubit-Verschränkungs-Gate direkt anwenden kannst.
examples.why: The English is about applying a gate to a qubit pair; the German turns the gate into the means of connecting the pair, which blurs what a coupling-map edge actually encodes.

examples.source: we are ready to calculate the median errors for the 'sx' and the 'ecr' gates
examples.translation: können wir die mittleren Fehler für die Gates 'sx' und 'ecr' berechnen
examples.suggested: können wir die Medianfehler (den Median der Fehler) für die Gates 'sx' und 'ecr' berechnen
examples.why: 'mittlere Fehler' reads as arithmetic mean, while the code uses statistics.median and prints 'Median SX error'; the file itself uses 'Median der T1-Zeiten' correctly earlier, so this is an internal inconsistency.

examples.source: the errors of readout tend to be larger than those of the 2-qubit operation, which in turn tend to be larger than the 1-qubit operation
examples.translation: sind die Auslesefehler in der Regel größer als die Fehler bei 2-Qubit-Operationen, die wiederum größer sind als die Fehler bei 1-Qubit-Operationen
examples.suggested: … die wiederum in der Regel größer sind als die Fehler bei 1-Qubit-Operationen
examples.why: The second hedge ('tend to') is dropped, turning a tendency into an unqualified statement about the 2-qubit vs 1-qubit ordering.

examples.source: A popular feature of Qiskit is its visualization capability.
examples.translation: Ein besonders beliebtes Feature von Qiskit ist seine Visualisierungsfähigkeit.
examples.suggested: Ein beliebtes Feature von Qiskit ist seine Visualisierungsfähigkeit.
examples.why: 'besonders' adds an emphasis the English does not make; minor claim-strengthening in an otherwise neutral appendix opener.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every substantive passage (the heavy-hex degree-3 vs. degree-4 argument in §3, the do-while fixed-point description in §3.4, the "Nicht jede einzelne Stufe kann immer unabhängig ausgeführt werden" caveat) is faithful, and the du-register holds throughout. The main editorial defect is a terminology collision: the transpiler's *stage* and `optimization_level` are both rendered "Stufe", so §2.1 "Optimierungsstufe" (= level) and §3.4 "Optimierungsstufe" (= stage) are identical headings for two different concepts, and §4.1 compounds it with "Vergleiche den Optimierungsstufenablauf für Stufe 2 mit dem obigen für Stufe 1" — "Phase" for stage would fix this. Second, "circuit" is rendered three ways in one file: the H1 says "Optimierung von Quantenschaltkreisen", §2–§3 consistently keep "Circuit", and §4.2 switches to "Schaltung/Schaltungen" in the very sentence that §2.1 rendered with "Circuits". Third, two calques: "happens to have no functions" → "verfügt zufällig über keine Funktionen" (a native writer would drop "zufällig") and "kopplungsbeschränkungsbewusste Circuit-Synthese". None of these would teach a learner something false.

examples.source: ### 3.4 Optimization Stage … The last default stage in the pipeline is optimization.
examples.translation: ### 3.4 Optimierungsstufe … Die letzte Standard-Stufe in der Pipeline ist die Optimierung.
examples.suggested: ### 3.4 Optimierungsphase … Die letzte Standardphase in der Pipeline ist die Optimierung.
examples.why: "Stufe" is already used for optimization_level (§2.1 heading is also "Optimierungsstufe", plus "Stufe 0"…"Stufe 3"), so the pipeline stage and the optimization level become the same word. §4.1's "Vergleiche den Optimierungsstufenablauf für Stufe 2 mit dem obigen für Stufe 1" mixes both senses inside one clause. Reserving "Phase" for stage removes the collision.

examples.source: We transpile the circuit without optimization (`optimization_level=0`) … there is a big difference in the circuit length of transpiled circuits.
examples.translation: Wir transpilieren die Schaltung ohne Optimierung (`optimization_level=0`) … einen großen Unterschied in der Länge der transpilierten Schaltungen.
examples.suggested: Wir transpilieren den Circuit ohne Optimierung … einen großen Unterschied in der Länge der transpilierten Circuits.
examples.why: The identical sentence in §2.1 (line 107-108) uses "Circuit"/"Circuits"; here it flips to "Schaltung", and the page H1 uses a third variant ("Quantenschaltkreisen"). One convention should hold across the file.

examples.source: Qiskit transpiler happens to have no functions of synthesizing GHZ state preparation circuit.
examples.translation: Der Qiskit-Transpiler verfügt zufällig über keine Funktionen zur Synthese von GHZ-Zustandspräparations-Circuits.
examples.suggested: Der Qiskit-Transpiler bietet keine Funktionen zur Synthese von GHZ-Zustandspräparations-Circuits.
examples.why: "zufällig" is a literal calque of "happens to"; in German it reads as "by coincidence", which is not what the English idiom conveys. Dropping it keeps the meaning and sounds like a German technical writer.

examples.source: a manual "coupling constraint-aware" circuit synthesis
examples.translation: eine manuelle „kopplungsbeschränkungsbewusste" Circuit-Synthese
examples.suggested: eine manuelle Circuit-Synthese, die die Kopplungsbeschränkungen berücksichtigt
examples.why: The 30-letter adjective compound is a mechanical calque of the English hyphenated modifier; German prefers a relative clause here. Meaning is intact, so this is style only.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the QFT product expansion, the |5⟩ rotation counts (5/8, 10/8 ≙ 1/4, 20/8 ≙ 1/2), the θ = 1/2³ = 1/8 readout and the Shor sentence all match the English, and the informal "du" register holds without a single Sie-slip. Four editorial slips: (1) "computational basis" is rendered three ways within the file — "Rechenbasisdarstellungen" (l.33), "Rechengrundlage (Z-Basis)" (l.82) and the correct "Rechenbasis" (l.86, 92); "Rechengrundlage" is a wrong word for the linear-algebra basis and lands exactly where the concept is introduced, though the "(Z-Basis)" gloss keeps it identifiable. (2) The "only if" of the controlled unitary is flattened to plain "wenn" (l.379), dropping the exclusivity qualifier. (3) "das linkeste Qubit" / "das rechteste" (l.88, 105, 107) is non-standard German; a native technical writer writes "das am weitesten links stehende Qubit" / "das äußerste rechte". (4) "was als Dezimalzahl `1` ergibt" (l.486) is ungrammatical-sounding; "was der Dezimalzahl 1 entspricht" is the natural phrasing. None of these would give a learner a false belief.

examples.source: The quantum Fourier transform (QFT) transforms between two bases, the computational (Z) basis, and the Fourier basis.
examples.translation: Die Quanten-Fourier-Transformation (QFT) transformiert zwischen zwei Basen: der Rechengrundlage (Z-Basis) und der Fourier-Basis.
examples.suggested: … zwischen zwei Basen: der Rechenbasis (Z-Basis) und der Fourier-Basis.
examples.why: "Rechengrundlage" means "basis for calculation" in the everyday sense, not the linear-algebra basis; the same term is correctly rendered "Rechenbasis" four lines later (l.86) and inside the math on l.92, so the file splits the core term at the very point where it is being defined.

examples.source: the controlled unitary $CU$ that applies the unitary operator $U$ on the target register only if its corresponding control bit is $|1\rangle$
examples.translation: das den unitären Operator $U$ auf das Zielregister anwendet, wenn das entsprechende Steuer-Bit $|1\rangle$ ist
examples.suggested: … anwendet, nur wenn das entsprechende Steuer-Bit $|1\rangle$ ist
examples.why: The exclusivity qualifier "only" is dropped; plain "wenn" states a sufficient condition where the English states a necessary-and-sufficient one. The operational meaning of a controlled gate still comes across, so this is a dropped qualifier rather than an inverted condition.

examples.source: the leftmost qubit flips with every increment … The leftmost qubit (`qubit 0`) in this case has the lowest frequency, and the rightmost the highest.
examples.translation: Das linkeste Qubit wechselt bei jeder Erhöhung der Zahl … Das linkeste Qubit (`qubit 0`) hat in diesem Fall die niedrigste Frequenz, das rechteste die höchste.
examples.suggested: Das am weitesten links stehende Qubit … das am weitesten rechts stehende die höchste.
examples.why: "linkeste"/"rechteste" are non-standard superlatives that no German technical writer would use; they mark the text as translated. Meaning is unaffected.

examples.source: We see we get one result (`001`) with certainty, which translates to the decimal: `1`.
examples.translation: Wir erhalten ein Ergebnis (`001`) mit Sicherheit, was als Dezimalzahl `1` ergibt.
examples.suggested: Wir erhalten mit Sicherheit genau ein Ergebnis (`001`), was der Dezimalzahl `1` entspricht.
examples.why: "was als Dezimalzahl 1 ergibt" is a broken construction (ergeben needs an object, not "als"), and unstressed "ein Ergebnis" loses the English emphasis on exactly one outcome.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — both protocols, both correction tables (00/01/10/11 → nothing/X/Z/iY=ZX for Bob, nothing/Z/X/ZX for Alice), the little-endian reading of the histogram, the no-cloning and FTL answers, and the tomography derivation all match the English exactly, and the informal "du" register holds. Four editorial slips remain. (1) The bullet gloss of teleportation softens the source's "requiring supplemental classical communication" to "– ergänzt durch klassische Kommunikation", turning a necessary condition into an optional add-on; the necessity is only recovered later in §4.5. (2) "In particular, dynamic circuits *tend to* have a higher error rate" loses its hedge and becomes the flat "Insbesondere haben dynamische Circuits eine höhere Fehlerrate". (3) A grammatical gender error: "Wähle den Backend mit der kürzesten Warteschlange" (should be "das Backend"). (4) "Quantum superdense coding" is calqued as "Quantensuperdense Coding" (intro bullet and summary bullet) while the body consistently says "Superdense Coding" — the hybrid form is not German and is inconsistent within the file; "circuit" likewise alternates between "Quantenschaltkreis" (headings 4.2, 5.2, Step 1) and "Circuit" (body, e.g. "Teleportations-Circuit"). None of these would make a learner form a false belief.

examples.source: Using a shared entangled state (sometimes called an e-bit) to send an unknown quantum state to a distant friend, requiring supplemental classical communication.
examples.translation: Verwendung eines gemeinsam genutzten verschränkten Zustands (manchmal als E-Bit bezeichnet), um einen unbekannten Quantenzustand an einen entfernten Freund zu senden – ergänzt durch klassische Kommunikation.
examples.suggested: … zu senden – wobei zusätzlich klassische Kommunikation erforderlich ist.
examples.why: "requiring" is a necessary condition (and the reason teleportation cannot beat light speed, per §4.5); "ergänzt durch" reads as an optional supplement and flattens the pedagogical point.

examples.source: In particular, dynamic circuits tend to have a higher error rate because of the time-consuming measurement in the middle of the circuit.
examples.translation: Insbesondere haben dynamische Circuits eine höhere Fehlerrate, weil die Messung mitten im Circuit zeitaufwendig ist.
examples.suggested: Insbesondere neigen dynamische Circuits zu einer höheren Fehlerrate, weil …
examples.why: The English hedge "tend to" is dropped, turning a tendency into a categorical property of dynamic circuits.

examples.source: Quantum superdense coding
examples.translation: Quantensuperdense Coding
examples.suggested: Superdense Coding (Quantum-Superdense-Coding)
examples.why: "Quantensuperdense" is a non-word: a German prefix welded onto an English adjective. The body of the file uses plain "Superdense Coding" (§5, §5.1, §5.2), so the compound is also internally inconsistent.

examples.source: Select the backend with the fewest number of jobs in the queue.
examples.translation: Wähle den Backend mit der kürzesten Warteschlange.
examples.suggested: Wähle das Backend mit der kürzesten Warteschlange.
examples.why: Wrong grammatical gender — "Backend" is neuter in German technical usage; "den Backend" is ungrammatical and immediately marks the text as non-native.

examples.source: quantum circuit / circuit
examples.translation: „Quantenschaltkreis" in headings (§4.2, §5.2, Schritt 1) vs. „Circuit" in the body („einen Circuit mit drei Qubits", „Quantenteleportations-Circuit", „Teleportations-Circuit")
examples.suggested: Pick one convention (either Quantenschaltkreis throughout, or Circuit throughout) and use it in both headings and body.
examples.why: Both renderings are defensible on their own, but alternating them within one lesson — sometimes in adjacent sentences — makes the text read as assembled rather than written.

editor_note: The core error-mitigation contrast of the lesson is destroyed: "mitigated"/"unmitigated" are rendered as the non-words „mittelten" / „unmittelten" (§1.1 line 57, §5.3 line 466, closing line 496). A German reader parses these against the real verb "mitteln" = "to average", so "Wir stellen die Werte für die „mittelten" Punkte aus Figure 4b bereit" reads as "the averaged points" — teaching that the paper's Figure 4b curve differs from the learner's by averaging rather than by error mitigation, which is the paper's whole novelty. The file itself proves the correct wording exists ("Zero-Noise-Extrapolation (ZNE) mit probabilistischer Fehlerverstärkung (PEA) zur Fehlerminderung", line 49), so the fix is fehlergemindert/fehlerkorrigiert or keeping the English "mitigated"/"unmitigated" in quotes. Secondary, non-misleading slips: "time dynamics of the Hamiltonian" becomes "Spindynamik des Hamiltonians" (line 29), duplicating the next sentence's "Spindynamik"; "Let us make a random use of the newly-defined rzz" becomes "Machen wir eine erste Verwendung" (line 142); and the calques "Die Wandzeit betrug 161 ms" (line 347) and "in Anwesenheit von Rauschen" (line 498, should be "in Gegenwart von Rauschen"/"trotz Rauschens") read as MT.

examples.source: We provide the values for the "mitigated" points in Figure 4b of the utility paper.
examples.translation: Wir stellen die Werte für die „mittelten" Punkte aus Figure 4b des Utility-Papers bereit.
examples.suggested: Wir stellen die Werte für die „fehlergeminderten" (mitigated) Punkte aus Figure 4b des Utility-Papers bereit.
examples.why: „mittelten" is not a German word in this form; the nearest real verb is "mitteln" (to average), so the learner reads "averaged points" and loses the error-mitigation contrast that is the entire point of the comparison. Same defect at line 57 (die „unmittelten" Punkte selbst darstellen) and line 496 (Ähneln deine Ergebnisse den „unmittelten" Punkten).

examples.source: In particular, they consider time dynamics of the Hamiltonian,
examples.translation: Konkret betrachten die Autoren die Spindynamik des Hamiltonians:
examples.suggested: Konkret betrachten die Autoren die Zeitdynamik des Hamiltonians:
examples.why: "time dynamics" is silently swapped for "Spindynamik", which then repeats verbatim in the next sentence ("Die Spindynamik wird von einem Anfangszustand aus … simuliert"). Not false, but the time-evolution framing the whole Trotter section builds on is flattened.

examples.source: Let us make a random use of the newly-defined `rzz`.
examples.translation: Machen wir eine erste Verwendung des neu definierten `rzz`.
examples.suggested: Verwenden wir das neu definierte `rzz` einmal beliebig.
examples.why: "random" (an arbitrary throwaway example) becomes "erste" (first), which reads as if this were a canonical first application rather than an ad-hoc demo.

examples.source: scientists across the globe have put forth tremendous ingenuity to extracting meaningful results even in the presence of noise
examples.translation: haben Wissenschaftlerinnen und Wissenschaftler auf der ganzen Welt großen Einfallsreichtum aufgewendet, um selbst in Anwesenheit von Rauschen aussagekräftige Ergebnisse zu extrahieren
examples.suggested: … um selbst trotz Rauschens aussagekräftige Ergebnisse zu gewinnen
examples.why: "in Anwesenheit von" is used of people in German; for a physical effect a native technical writer writes "in Gegenwart von Rauschen" or "trotz Rauschens". Same class as "Die Wandzeit betrug 161 ms" (line 347), a calque of "wall time" where German uses "Laufzeit"/"Wall-Clock-Zeit".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the Trotterisierung derivation, the commuting/non-commuting distinction ("Wenn Operatoren jedoch nicht vertauschen …"), the N=2/N=6 lattice sizes, +1/−1 magnetization, the 20- vs. 70-Qubit setups and the MPS-as-reference framing all match the English, and the informal "du" register holds ("Erstelle …", "Versuche es selbst", "Du hast …"). What a native editor would still change is terminology consistency: "circuit" is rendered four ways in one file — "Quantencircuit" (§ Anfangszustand), bare "Circuit", "Quantum Circuit" (Aufgabe 4 heading, § 3.1) and once "Schaltkreis" (line 450) — and "Hamiltonian" appears as heading "Den Hamiltonian definieren" (line 393) against "Hamiltonoperator" everywhere else. The closing sentence renders "utility-scale quantum journey" as "Reise in die Quantum-Computing-Nutzungsphase" and pairs it with the un-idiomatic "einen weiteren Schritt … zurückgelegt", where the page title itself keeps "Utility-scale". Smaller: "for convenience" became "zur Übersicht" (line 33), the German closing quotes in Aufgabe 1 are straight ASCII („Anzahl der Qubits"), and the final image alt text (line 859) is still English "Output of the previous code cell" while every other one is "Ausgabe der vorherigen Code-Zelle". None of these mislead a learner.

examples.source: We here construct a circuit for a single time step using Lie–Trotter. / Prepare the quantum circuit 2 (Single circuit for time evolution)
examples.translation: "Quantencircuit vorbereiten 2 (Einzelner Circuit …)" (L203) vs. "Den Quantum Circuit 2 vorbereiten …" (L449) vs. "Hier konstruieren wir einen Schaltkreis …" (L450) vs. "der korrekten Quantum Circuits" (L592)
examples.suggested: Pick one convention — e.g. "Quantencircuit" for the compound and "Circuit" standalone — and drop "Schaltkreis" and "Quantum Circuit".
examples.why: Four renderings of the same core term inside one lesson; the concept stays identifiable, so this is a consistency slip rather than a meaning defect.

examples.source: #### Define the Hamiltonian (both the 20-qubit and the 70-qubit section)
examples.translation: L163 "#### Definition des Hamiltonoperators" vs. L393 "#### Den Hamiltonian definieren"
examples.suggested: "Den Hamiltonoperator definieren" in both places.
examples.why: The same English heading is translated two different ways; "Hamiltonoperator" is the term used in all the body prose, so the lone "Hamiltonian" heading reads as an oversight.

examples.source: Congratulations! You have moved one step further in your utility-scale quantum journey.
examples.translation: Herzlichen Glückwunsch! Du hast einen weiteren Schritt auf deiner Reise in die Quantum-Computing-Nutzungsphase zurückgelegt.
examples.suggested: Herzlichen Glückwunsch! Du bist auf deiner Reise zum Quantencomputing im Utility-Maßstab einen Schritt weitergekommen.
examples.why: "Nutzungsphase" is an invented gloss for the term of art "utility-scale" (which the page title itself keeps as "Utility-scale"), and "einen Schritt zurücklegen" is not idiomatic German — one legt eine Strecke zurück, geht aber einen Schritt weiter.

examples.source: We repeat that discussion here for convenience.
examples.translation: Wir wiederholen diese Diskussion hier zur Übersicht.
examples.suggested: Wir wiederholen diese Ausführungen hier der Einfachheit halber.
examples.why: "zur Übersicht" (for an overview) shifts the reason for the repetition from reader convenience to providing a summary; harmless for comprehension but a needless drift.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked every claim-bearing sentence including the tricky ones (the "> 50%" goal, "Die Tiefe dieses Baums betraegt 5/6", and the counter-intuitive "Ueberraschenderweise hat sich die Zwei-Qubit-Tiefe von 9 auf 8 verringert, obwohl die Baumtiefe von 5 auf 6 gestiegen ist!", which correctly mirrors the English even where the English disagrees with its own printed output) — and found no drift, no inverted condition, no hallucinated sentence, and no dropped caveat; core terms (Qubit, Gate, Circuit, Fidelity, Backend, Shots, transpilieren, Kopplungskarte, Wurzelknoten, Breitensuche) are correct and consistent, and "du" holds everywhere. The dominant defect is orthographic and file-wide: the German is written in umlaut-free ASCII transliteration ("Einfuehrung", "fuer", "waehlen", "hoechsten", "erfuellt", "gross", "weisst"), and this is baked into the PO source (i18n/de/po/.../utility-iii.po), not a rendering artifact — every one of the 14 sibling files in this course uses proper ü/ä/ö (teleportation.mdx 209, utility-ii.mdx 110), this file has exactly 0. Secondary: two calqued sentences that a native technical writer would recast ("Lass uns kurz GHZ-Zustaende wiederholen und welche Art von Verteilung du ... erwarten koenntest", and the link-fragment "[PDF herunterladen](...) der Originalvorlesung."), plus a term split where "circuit" is normally kept as "Circuit" but becomes "Quantenschaltkreis" in two places.

examples.source: Introduction / for / choose / The depth is not too large
examples.translation: Einfuehrung / fuer / waehlen / Die Tiefe ist nicht allzu gross
examples.suggested: Einführung / für / wählen / … nicht allzu groß
examples.why: The entire file is written without umlauts or ß, using ASCII digraphs (ue/ae/oe) and ss. It is legible but reads as broken German typography and is inconsistent with the rest of the de locale: all 14 sibling files in this course use proper ü/ä/ö, this one has zero. Confirmed to originate in the PO msgstrs, so it is a translation defect, not a build artifact.

examples.source: Let us briefly review GHZ states, and what sort of distribution you might expect from ```Sampler``` applied to one.
examples.translation: Lass uns kurz GHZ-Zustaende wiederholen und welche Art von Verteilung du von ```Sampler``` angewendet auf einen solchen Zustand erwarten koenntest.
examples.suggested: Wiederholen wir kurz die GHZ-Zustände und sehen wir uns an, welche Verteilung du von ```Sampler``` erwarten kannst, wenn er auf einen solchen Zustand angewendet wird.
examples.why: Calqued English coordination: the imperative object 'GHZ-Zustaende wiederholen' is joined to an indirect question ('und welche Art von Verteilung …') with no governing verb, which does not work in German. The participle insert 'von Sampler angewendet auf einen solchen Zustand' is likewise raw English word order.

examples.source: [Download the pdf](…) of the original lecture.
examples.translation: [PDF herunterladen](…) der Originalvorlesung.
examples.suggested: [Lade das PDF](…) der Originalvorlesung herunter.
examples.why: The separable verb was pulled inside the link text, leaving 'der Originalvorlesung' dangling after a complete imperative; a German reader parses the sentence twice. No meaning is lost, but no native writer would leave it.

examples.source: quantum circuit / this circuit / Map problem to quantum circuits and operators
examples.translation: Quantenschaltkreis / diesen Circuit / Problem auf Quantenschaltkreise und Operatoren abbilden
examples.suggested: Pick one convention — given that the file otherwise keeps 'Circuit' (GHZ-Circuit, Circuit-Tiefe), use 'Quantencircuit' or simply 'Circuit' in these two spots as well.
examples.why: Within-file split: 'circuit' is kept as the English term everywhere (GHZ-Circuit, ghz1-Circuit, Circuit-Tiefe) except in two places where it becomes 'Quantenschaltkreis'. The concept stays perfectly identifiable, so this is cosmetic consistency, not a comprehension risk.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no semantic drift, no inverted condition, no swapped quantity and no hallucinated claim; the tricky passages (x_i=0 ⇒ z_i=1, dropping the 1/4 prefactor and the n² offset, "four bitstrings distinctly more likely", "the cut value of the optimal solution is 5") all survive intact, and core terms are right and consistent (Erwartungswert, Grundzustand, Hamiltonoperator, Einheitsmatrix, Transponierte, Ansatz/Gates/Circuit kept English). The dominant defect is orthographic/naturalness: virtually every umlaut is written as an ASCII digraph (Ueberblick, Loesung, koennen, moeglicherweise, fuer, naechst-), which is an outlier for this locale — 116 digraph lines and only 8 real umlauts here, while every sibling page in the same course (teleportation 222, bits-gates-and-circuits 158, quantum-phase-estimation 109) uses proper umlauts — and it is internally inconsistent, e.g. heading 3.4 "Ausführung" vs heading "Ausfuehrung" three headings later, and "hängt/durchführen/Für" in §"Definiere Backend" next to digraphs everywhere else. On top of that: an outright typo "zunachst" (line ~590, neither umlaut nor digraph), a subordinate-clause word-order slip "dass wenn $x_i$ gleich $0$ ist, dann muss $z_i$ gleich $1$ sein", "sampling-based quantum diagonalization" rendered "probenbasierte Quantendiagonalisierung" (should be stichprobenbasiert; "Probe" is a specimen, not a statistical sample), and two English calques ("befoerdere die $z_i$-Variablen", "Wir muessen durch Parameter suchen"). None of these would mislead a learner, so MINOR_ISSUES, not FAIL.

examples.source: This tutorial provides an overview of a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm

No native German technical writer does this in prose, and it is an outlier for the locale: this page has 116 digraph lines / 8 real umlauts, while sibling pages in the same course (teleportation.mdx 222 umlauts, bits-gates-and-circuits.mdx 158) are written correctly.

examples.source: by first considering the minimization of a function $f(x)$

examples.source: sampling-based quantum diagonalization (SQD)
examples.translation: probenbasierte Quantendiagonalisierung (SQD)
examples.suggested: stichprobenbasierte Quantendiagonalisierung (SQD)
examples.why: 'Probe' in German means a specimen/sample of material; the statistical sense required here is 'Stichprobe'. Recognizable from the SQD acronym, so not misleading, but it is the wrong German word for the concept — note the same file correctly uses 'Sampeln'/'Sampling' elsewhere.

examples.source: promote the $z_i$ variables to a Pauli $Z$ matrix … We will need to search through parameters and find those that yield the lowest eigenvalue.
examples.translation: befoerdere die $z_i$-Variablen zu einer Pauli-$Z$-Matrix … Wir muessen durch Parameter suchen und diejenigen finden, die den niedrigsten Eigenwert liefern.
examples.suggested: hebe die $z_i$-Variablen zu einer Pauli-$Z$-Matrix an … Wir müssen den Parameterraum durchsuchen und die Werte finden, die den niedrigsten Eigenwert liefern.
examples.why: Two English calques. 'befördern' in German means promoting a person or transporting cargo, never lifting a variable to an operator; 'durch Parameter suchen' is a word-for-word rendering of 'search through parameters' that a German technical writer would phrase as 'den Parameterraum durchsuchen'.

editor_note: No misleading drift: every quantitative claim, condition and caveat survives intact (Sparse/Poly(n)-Effizienzbedingung, $4^n$-Pauli-Zerlegung, "Wahrscheinlichkeiten stammen aus $V|\psi\rangle$ und nicht aus $|\psi\rangle$", Minima-statt-Maxima-Vorzeichenwechsel, Open-Plan/Fehlercode-1217-Hinweis), the "du"-Register holds throughout, and core terms are right (Erwartungswert, Observable, Eigenzustand, Rechenbasis, Shots, Fehlerunterdrückung/Fehlerminderung). What a native technical editor would change: (a) "native basis gates" is rendered "native Basistransformationen" (§ISA-Absatz), which names a change of basis rather than the device's Gate-Satz — and it contradicts the correct "nativen Gates des Quantensystems" three paragraphs earlier; (b) "circuit" is split four ways — "Circuit" (dominant), "Quantenkreis", "Hilfsschaltkreise", "Schaltkreis…" — within one file; (c) "mitigate errors in the raw results" becomes "Fehler … zu korrigieren", conflating Fehlerminderung with Fehlerkorrektur in the very lesson that contrasts them. Plus small mechanical slips: "Rechenbasisszustand" (doubled s, 2×), "was einem Teilmenge … entspricht", "des Ziel-Observablen … seine Diagonalisierung" (Observable is feminine), the heading "Mathematical rigor" softened to "Mathematische Grundlagen", an added clause "die messbare Größen repräsentieren" not in the source, and one DefinitionTooltip ("A Hermitian is a square matrix…") left entirely in English while all sibling tooltips are translated.

examples.source: These target constraints are defined by factors like the device’s native basis gates, its qubit connectivity, and - when relevant - its pulse and other instruction timing specifications.
examples.translation: Diese Zieleinschränkungen werden durch Faktoren wie die nativen Basistransformationen des Geräts, seine Qubit-Konnektivität und – wenn relevant – seine Puls- und andere Instruktions-Timing-Spezifikationen definiert.
examples.suggested: … durch Faktoren wie die nativen Basis-Gates des Geräts, seine Qubit-Konnektivität …
examples.why: "Basis gates" is the device's native gate set; "Basistransformationen" reads as a change of basis — a different concept, and inconsistent with the correct "nativen Gates des Quantensystems" used in the Fehlerunterdrückung list just above.

examples.source: …classical post-processing overhead to mitigate errors in the raw results by using the generated model.
examples.translation: …sowie ein klassischer Nachverarbeitungs-Overhead, um Fehler in den Rohergebnissen mithilfe des erstellten Modells zu korrigieren.
examples.suggested: …um Fehler in den Rohergebnissen mithilfe des erstellten Modells abzumildern (zu mindern).
examples.why: The lesson explicitly distinguishes Fehlerminderung from Fehlerkorrektur (the Quantenvorteil-Grafik names Quantenfehlerkorrektur separately); rendering "mitigate" as "korrigieren" blurs exactly that distinction.

examples.source: quantum circuit / auxiliary circuits / runs the circuit multiple times
examples.translation: „…wenn ein Quantenkreis den Zustand $|\psi\rangle$ präpariert" … „Deshalb brauchen wir Hilfsschaltkreise" … „führt den Circuit mehrfach … aus"
examples.suggested: Pick one convention (the file's dominant "Circuit"): „…wenn ein Circuit den Zustand präpariert" / „…brauchen wir Hilfs-Circuits".
examples.why: Three renderings of the same object inside one lesson (Quantenkreis / Schaltkreis / Circuit); recognizable, but a native technical editor would unify them.

examples.source: …the probability of each possible computational basis state. … a subsection of the circuit, representing a subset of the total possible states.
examples.translation: …die Wahrscheinlichkeit jedes möglichen Rechenbasisszustands. … was einem Teilmenge aller möglichen Zustände entspricht.
examples.suggested: …jedes möglichen Rechenbasiszustands … was einer Teilmenge aller möglichen Zustände entspricht.
examples.why: Spelling slip "Rechenbasisszustand" (doubled s, also in "Rechenbasisszuständen") and a wrong article/gender "einem Teilmenge" — mechanical errors a German technical writer would not leave.

examples.source: ### Mathematical rigor (optional)  …  we can also describe the state of a quantum system using *observables*, which are mathematical objects.
examples.translation: ### Mathematische Grundlagen (optional)  …  kann auch der Zustand eines Quantensystems durch *Observablen* beschrieben werden – mathematische Objekte, die messbare Größen repräsentieren.
examples.suggested: ### Mathematische Strenge (optional) / Mathematisch exakte Herleitung (optional)  …  durch *Observablen* beschrieben werden – mathematische Objekte.
examples.why: "Grundlagen" (basics) inverts the heading's promise of an optional rigorous derivation, and the observables sentence gains a clause ("die messbare Größen repräsentieren") that is not in the source; both are true-but-added/softened, not misleading.

examples.source: Given that $\hat{H}$ is <DefinitionTooltip definition="A Hermitian is a square matrix that is equal to its own conjugate transpose, or a linear operator that is self-adjoint.">Hermitian</DefinitionTooltip>
examples.translation: Da $\hat{H}$ <DefinitionTooltip definition="A Hermitian is a square matrix that is equal to its own conjugate transpose, or a linear operator that is self-adjoint.">hermitesch</DefinitionTooltip> ist
examples.suggested: definition="Eine hermitesche Matrix ist eine quadratische Matrix, die gleich ihrer eigenen konjugiert Transponierten ist, bzw. ein selbstadjungierter linearer Operator."
examples.why: Every other DefinitionTooltip in the file (Primitives, Pauli-Operatoren, Sampling, Black Box, Overhead, Bias) is translated; this one tooltip still shows an English sentence to the German reader. Same sentence also carries the gender slips "des Ziel-Observablen … seine Diagonalisierung" (should be "der Ziel-Observablen … ihre").

editor_note: No misleading content: every truth table, the little-endian convention, the CNOT/Toffoli control-target wording ("nur dann ... wenn *beide* Kontroll-Qubits im Zustand |1⟩ sind"), the global-vs-relative-phase passage, and all nine deliberately true/false quiz statements (2, 3, 4, 5, 8 keep their falseness intact) survive faithfully, and "du" holds throughout. What a native editor would change is consistency and polish. (1) The core term "circuit" is split down the middle of the file: "Quantenschaltung", "Halb-Addierer-Schaltung", "Schaltkreisdiagramm" and the heading "### Schaltungen:" in the classical half, then "Circuit", "Quantencircuit", "Circuit-Diagramm", "Halbaddierer-Circuit" and the heading "## Circuits" from the Messungen section onward — the same for "Gate" vs "Gatter" ("Quanten-Gates" but "Quantengatter", "klassischen Zwei-Bit-Gattern", "nativen Gatter"), and the repeated EN heading "Check your understanding" alternates between "Verständnisfragen" (first four) and "Teste dein Verständnis" (last four). (2) Two typos in terminology: "Vektordarlstellungen" (should be Vektordarstellungen) and "Rechenbasisstands" (should be Rechenbasiszustands), plus "Rechenbasis-Zustände" vs "Rechenbasiszuständen". (3) Non-native superlatives "rechteste"/"linkste"/"linksten Position" where German uses "am weitesten rechts/links stehend" or "höchstwertig", and the gender slip "einer der CNOT-Gates" (Gate is neuter → "eines der CNOT-Gates"). (4) Two mild qualifier losses that do not change the meaning taught: OR's "*either* of the bits are 1" becomes "*eines* der Bits" without "mindestens" (the truth table directly below disambiguates), and "Two-qubit gates *can* resemble ... with one important caveat" becomes the flat "ähneln ..., haben jedoch einen wichtigen Unterschied".

examples.source: ### Circuits:  …  ## Circuits
examples.translation: ### Schaltungen: {#circuits}  …  ## Circuits {#circuits-1}
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering for the whole file (e.g. "Schaltung/Quantenschaltung" or "Circuit/Quantencircuit") and use it in headings and body alike; likewise "Halb-Addierer-Schaltung" vs "Halbaddierer-Circuit".
examples.why: The file's central object is named two different ways in two halves — classical part in German, quantum part in English — so a learner meets "Schaltkreisdiagramm" (line 144) and "Circuit-Diagramm" (line 416/619) for the same picture. Identifiable, hence MINOR, but a native editor would unify it.

examples.source: quantum gates / classical gates / native set of gates
examples.translation: "Quanten-Gates" (296) but "Alle Quantengatter müssen reversibel sein" (391), "klassischen Zwei-Bit-Gattern" (391), "Da Quantengatter *reversibel* sind" (562), "schreibt die Gates in die nativen Gatter um" (629), "**Quantengatter** sind reversible Operationen" (779)
examples.suggested: Choose "Gate" (Qiskit-conventional) or "Gatter" (classic German EE term) and hold it; "schreibt die Gates in die nativen Gatter um" mixes both inside one clause.
examples.why: Both renderings are individually defensible, but alternating them — sometimes within a single sentence — is the kind of inconsistency a technical editor removes.

examples.source: the vector form of the states are chosen to be … the corresponding computational basis state
examples.translation: "Für ein einzelnes Qubit werden die Vektordarlstellungen der Zustände wie folgt gewählt" … "dem Quadrat der Amplitude des entsprechenden Rechenbasisstands"
examples.suggested: "Vektordarstellungen"; "des entsprechenden Rechenbasiszustands"
examples.why: Two straightforward typos in domain terms — one a letter transposition, one a malformed compound genitive that also breaks consistency with "Rechenbasis-Zustände" (line 212) and "Rechenbasiszuständen" (line 773).

examples.source: the least-significant (rightmost) bit … the most significant (leftmost bit) … places the least significant qubit, q_0, in the rightmost position
examples.translation: "das am wenigsten signifikante (rechteste) Bit" … "das bedeutendste (linkste) Bit" … "an der rechtesten Position und das signifikanteste Qubit, $q_N$, an der linksten Position"
examples.suggested: "das niederwertigste (am weitesten rechts stehende) Bit" … "das höchstwertige (am weitesten links stehende) Bit" … "ganz rechts … ganz links"
examples.why: "rechteste", "linkste", "linksten" are not idiomatic German superlatives; no native technical writer would form them, and the file itself uses the correct "ganz rechts / ganz links" a few lines earlier (line 227, 393).

examples.source: OR is another two-bit gate with a single output bit. It outputs 1 if *either* of the bits are 1:
examples.translation: OR ist ein weiteres Zwei-Bit-Gate mit einem einzelnen Ausgangsbit. Es gibt 1 aus, wenn *eines* der Bits 1 ist:
examples.suggested: … wenn *mindestens eines* der Bits 1 ist:
examples.why: "eines" loses the inclusive sense of "either" and sits awkwardly against the XOR definition three paragraphs later ("*genau eines*"), inviting the reader to hear an exclusive OR. The truth table immediately below (11 → 1) prevents an actual false belief, so this is a dropped qualifier, not a FAIL.

editor_note: The prose is otherwise fluent, faithful and consistently "du"-form, but one instruction is inverted: the English "you can uncomment the next code block, which will run the code on a local simulator" becomes "kannst du den nächsten Code-Block auskommentieren" (= comment it OUT) — the exact opposite of the required action, and the file itself gets the same instruction right later ("kommentiere ... den obigen Block ein", Experiment 2), so a learner who follows the German literally never enables the simulator fallback. Two further term slips: "base gates" is rendered "Basistransformationen" (the Qiskit term is "Basisgatter"; the file uses "Hadamard-Gate" elsewhere, so it is also internally inconsistent), and IBM's product name "Qiskit Classroom module" appears both as "Qiskit-Classrooms-Modul" and as the over-translated "Qiskit-Klassenzimmer-Modul". Finally, "yield similar numbers of 0 and 1 states (like similar numbers of spin up and spin down states)" is strengthened to "gleich viele Spin-up- und Spin-down-Zustände" (equal numbers), overstating a statistical result the 100-shot histogram does not show exactly.

examples.source: you can uncomment the next code block, which will run the code on a local simulator.
examples.translation: kannst du den nächsten Code-Block auskommentieren, der den Code auf einem lokalen Simulator ausführt.
examples.suggested: kannst du den nächsten Code-Block einkommentieren (die Kommentarzeichen entfernen); er führt den Code auf einem lokalen Simulator aus.
examples.why: 'auskommentieren' means to comment OUT — the inverse of 'uncomment'. The block is already fully commented, so following the German literally leaves the simulator fallback disabled. The parallel passage at DE line 399 correctly says 'kommentiere ... ein', proving this is an error, not a convention.

examples.source: we must map our circuit onto the base gates available to our chosen quantum computer
examples.translation: unseren Circuit auf die Basistransformationen des gewählten Quantencomputers abbilden
examples.suggested: unseren Circuit auf die Basisgatter des gewählten Quantencomputers abbilden
examples.why: 'Basistransformationen' is not the domain term; German Qiskit material says 'Basisgatter'. The file uses 'Hadamard-Gate' elsewhere, so the concept is also rendered inconsistently within the same page.

examples.source: See the Qiskit Classroom module on Bell's theorem
examples.translation: siehe das Qiskit-Klassenzimmer-Modul zum Bell-Theorem
examples.suggested: siehe das Qiskit-Classrooms-Modul zum Bellschen Theorem
examples.why: The same product name appears as 'Qiskit-in-Classrooms-Modul' (line 18), 'Qiskit-Classrooms-Modul' (line 203) and the over-translated 'Qiskit-Klassenzimmer-Modul' here; a proper name should not be translated, and the three-way split makes the cross-reference harder to follow.

examples.source: yield similar numbers of 0 and 1 states (like similar numbers of spin up and spin down states)
examples.translation: liefert ähnlich viele 0- und 1-Zustände (ähnlich wie gleich viele Spin-up- und Spin-down-Zustände)
examples.suggested: liefert ähnlich viele 0- und 1-Zustände (so wie ähnlich viele Spin-up- und Spin-down-Zustände)
examples.why: 'gleich viele' asserts equal counts where the English says only 'similar numbers'; it strengthens a statistical statement about a 100-shot histogram that only approximates 50/50.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat; the numeric claims (zwei Swaps … weitere zwei Swaps, drei CNOT-Gates → Sampling-Overhead von $9^3$, "um mehr als die Hälfte reduziert") all match the English, and the informal "du" register holds ("Du kannst entweder ein Fake-Backend …", "findest du im Erläuterungsmaterial"). What a native editor would change is consistency: "subexperiments" is rendered "Teilexperimente" everywhere (headings, Steps 2–4) except inside the **Hinweis** block, where it suddenly becomes "Subexperimente" — the concept stays identifiable, but the split is jarring in the one paragraph that most needs to read as part of the same text. Likewise "decomposition" alternates between "Gate-Dekomposition" (cut_gates paragraph) and "Zerlegung" ("bei der Zerlegung des Problems", "der zerlegten Gates"); "Zerlegung" is the more idiomatic German term and should carry both. Third, the framework name "Qiskit pattern" is over-translated to "Qiskit-Muster", where German quantum writing normally keeps "Qiskit Pattern" as the product name.

examples.source: Observable term coefficients and phases are ignored during decomposition of the problem and execution of the subexperiments.
examples.translation: Koeffizienten und Phasen der Observablen-Terme werden bei der Zerlegung des Problems und der Ausführung der Subexperimente ignoriert.
examples.suggested: … und der Ausführung der Teilexperimente ignoriert.
examples.why: Every other occurrence in the file (headings and Steps 2–4 body text) uses "Teilexperimente"; only this note switches to "Subexperimente". Within-file inconsistency for the file's central object.

examples.source: …and also return a list of `QPDBasis` instances -- one for each gate decomposition.
examples.translation: …und gibt außerdem eine Liste von `QPDBasis`-Instanzen zurück – eine für jede Gate-Dekomposition.
examples.suggested: … – eine für jede Gate-Zerlegung.
examples.why: "decomposition" is elsewhere rendered "Zerlegung" ("bei der Zerlegung des Problems", "der zerlegten Gates"); "Dekomposition" is the less idiomatic loan and makes the same concept look like two.

examples.source: These are the steps that we will take in this [Qiskit pattern](…):
examples.translation: Dies sind die Schritte, die wir in diesem [Qiskit-Muster](…) durchführen werden:
examples.suggested: … die wir in diesem [Qiskit Pattern](…) durchführen werden:
examples.why: "Qiskit patterns" is an IBM product/framework name that German quantum documentation keeps in English; "Qiskit-Muster" reads as a generic "pattern" and loses the pointer to the named workflow.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked the physics-bearing passages paragraph against paragraph (Clifford-angle caveat "Je weiter $h$ von einem Clifford-Winkel entfernt ist …, desto schwieriger", the noise_scales `0.0` rationale, the non-monotonicity caveats on max_err_terms/max_obs_terms, "nur die obersten 30 Terme … dennoch nützlich, ihm zu erlauben, groß zu werden") and found no inverted condition, swapped quantity, dropped caveat or hallucination; the informal "du" holds consistently (lernst du, musst du, Denk daran, findest du). What a native technical editor would still change is consistency: "observable" is given three different genders within the file — masculine ("eines Observablen", "den Observable durch diesen entwickelten Generator", "auf den Observable angewendet"), feminine ("Die Observable … um eine rauschmindernde Observable zu erhalten", "eine Observable angeben"), and a mixed neuter-ish "im rauschmitigierenden Observable $\tilde{O}$" — inside adjacent paragraphs of the same section.
